who: Robert C. Davis, historian of Renaissance Italy and the Mediterranean at Ohio State; PhD Johns Hopkins 1989.

evidence.says: Ohio State profile identifies his field and Johns Hopkins PhD (1989).
John M. Hunt’s 2009 Ohio State dissertation names Professor Robert C. Davis as advisor.
LC identifies Robert Charles Davis as author of Shipbuilders of the Venetian Arsenal and emeritus professor of Mediterranean history at Ohio State.
The other candidate, R. Chris Davis, wrote Certifiably Romanian as a 2012 Oxford history DPhil thesis.

notes: Matches Robert Charles Davis; R. Chris Davis is a different historian.

who: Sylvie Dépatie, historian of preindustrial Canada at UQAM; PhD in history, McGill.

evidence.says: UQAM profile gives a McGill history PhD and lists Arnaud Bessière’s 2007 domestic-service dissertation under supervised doctoral theses.
LC identifies Sylvie Dépatie, author of Contributions à l’étude du régime seigneurial canadien, as a professor at UQAM.

notes: Name, university, doctorate institution and named student agree.

who: Thomas R. Dunlap, historian at Texas A&M; PhD in history, Wisconsin–Madison 1975.

evidence.says: Institutional CV records a Wisconsin–Madison history PhD in 1975 and a Texas A&M professorship beginning in 1991.
Neall W. Pogue’s May 2016 dissertation, The Lost Environmentalists, names Thomas R. Dunlap as committee chair.
LC identifies Thomas R. Dunlap, author of DDT, and records his Wisconsin–Madison PhD in 1975.

notes: Exact doctorate and direct dissertation-chair evidence establish the match.

who: Ellen Dwyer, historian of medicine and criminal justice at Indiana University Bloomington; PhD Yale.

evidence.says: Indiana’s retirement tribute records her Yale PhD, history appointment from 1995, dissertation committee service, and authorship of Homes for the Mad.
Indiana History lists Ellen Dwyer as an emerita professor.
LC identifies Ellen Dwyer, author of Homes for the Mad, as an associate professor in Indiana University Bloomington’s Department of Criminal Justice.

notes: Authority record and university sources agree on institution and work; Hoshino’s supervision was not independently located.

who: William Gillette, historian of the Civil War, Reconstruction and New Jersey at Rutgers; PhD Princeton 1963.

evidence.says: Rutgers records his employment from 1967 to 2015, Princeton PhD, Reconstruction research, and The Right to Vote among his books.
Historical Society of Bloomfield identifies Rutgers emeritus historian William Gillette and dates his Princeton history doctorate to 1963.
LC identifies William Gillette through his book The Right to Vote (1965).

notes: Doctorate, Rutgers employment during 1999, field and authority-linked book agree.

who: Jason Glenn, historian of medieval Europe at USC; PhD in medieval history, Berkeley 1997.

evidence.says: USC profile records his Berkeley medieval-history PhD in May 1997, USC appointments beginning in 1998, and Politics and History in the Tenth Century.
LC identifies Jason Glenn, author of Politics and History in the Tenth Century, as an assistant professor of history at USC.

notes: Candidate’s institution, employment period, doctorate and field match; Wyman’s supervision was not independently located.

who: Kenneth W. Goings, historian of African American history, formerly at Memphis; PhD Princeton 1977.

evidence.says: Memphis History Happenings (Fall 2006), page 19, identifies David Jackson as a 1997 PhD and says Charles Crawford and Kenneth Goings guided his dissertation on Charles Banks.
LC identifies Kenneth W. Goings, an African American history professor at Ohio State, and records his Princeton PhD in 1977.

notes: Direct student-supervision evidence and exact doctorate support the match.

who: Jeremy A. Greene, historian of medicine at Johns Hopkins; PhD in history of science, Harvard 2005.

evidence.says: Johns Hopkins profile records Greene’s Harvard history-of-science PhD in 2005 and appointment in the Institute for the History of Medicine.
SHAFR’s April 2017 Passport names Jeremy Greene as adviser to Johns Hopkins doctoral candidate Heidi Morefield.
LC identifies Jeremy A. Greene, author of Prescribing by Numbers, as professor of medicine and history of medicine at Johns Hopkins.
The other candidate, J. Megan Greene, is a University of Kansas historian and author of The Origins of the Developmental State in Taiwan.

notes: Matches Jeremy A. Greene; J. Megan Greene is a different historian.
